151.name: Literal
151.docs:
Literals, e.g. `12u8`, `1.0e-40`, `b"123"`. Note that `_` is an invalid
suffix, but may be present here on string and float literals. Users of
this type will need to check for and reject that case.

See [LiteralKind] for more details.

402.name: is_horizontal_whitespace
402.docs: True if `c` is considered horizontal whitespace according to Rust language definition.

401.name: is_whitespace
401.docs:
True if `c` is considered a whitespace according to Rust language definition.
See [Rust language reference](https://doc.rust-lang.org/reference/whitespace.html)
for definitions of these classes.

23.name: into
23.docs: Calls `U::from(self)`. That is, this conversion is whatever the implementation of [From]<T> for U chooses to do.

48.name: Cursor
48.docs:
Peekable iterator over a char sequence.

Next characters can be peeked via `first` method,
and position can be shifted forward via `bump` method.

148.name: GuardedStrPrefix
148.docs:
Guarded string literal prefix: `#"` or `##`.

Used for reserving "guarded strings" (RFC 3598) in edition 2024.
Split into the component tokens on older editions.

399.name: tokenize
399.docs:
Creates an iterator that produces tokens from the input string.

When parsing a full Rust document,
first [`strip_shebang`] and then allow frontmatters with [`FrontmatterAllowed::Yes`].

When tokenizing a slice of a document, be sure to disallow frontmatters with [`FrontmatterAllowed::No`]

147.name: RawLifetime
147.docs:
A raw lifetime, e.g. `'r#foo`. In edition < 2021 it will be split into
several tokens: `'r` and `#` and `foo`.

398.name: validate_raw_str
398.docs:
Validates a raw string literal. Used for getting more information about a
problem with a `RawStr`/`RawByteStr` with a `None` field.

146.name: UnknownPrefixLifetime
146.docs:
An unknown prefix in a lifetime, like `'foo#`.

Like `UnknownPrefix`, only the `'` and prefix are included in the token
and not the separator.

397.name: strip_shebang
397.docs:
`rustc` allows files to have a shebang, e.g. "#!/usr/bin/rustrun",
but shebang isn't a part of rust syntax.

145.name: UnknownPrefix
145.docs:
An unknown literal prefix, like `foo#`, `foo'`, `foo"`. Excludes
literal prefixes that contain emoji, which are considered "invalid".

Note that only the
prefix (`foo`) is included in the token, not the separator (which is
lexed as its own distinct token). In Rust 2021 and later, reserved
prefixes are reported as errors; in earlier editions, they result in a
(allowed by default) lint, and are treated as regular identifier
tokens.

44.name: chars
44.docs: Iterator over chars. Slightly faster than a &str.

245.name: Base
245.docs: Base of numeric literal encoding according to its prefix.

143.name: InvalidIdent
143.docs: An identifier that is invalid because it contains emoji.

67.name: frontmatter
67.docs: Given that one `-` was eaten, eat the rest of the frontmatter.

142.name: Ident
142.docs: An identifier or keyword, e.g. `ident` or `continue`.

66.name: Token
66.docs:
Parsed token.
It doesn't contain information about data that has been parsed,
only the type of the token and its size.

65.name: advance_token
65.docs: Parses a token from the input string.

88.name: eat_float_exponent
88.docs:
Eats the float exponent. Returns true if at least one digit was met,
and returns false otherwise.

137.name: BlockComment
137.docs:
A block comment, e.g. `/* block comment */`.

Block comments can be recursive, so a sequence like `/* /* */`
will not be considered terminated and will result in a parsing error.

61.name: eat_while
61.docs: Eats symbols while predicate returns true or until the end of file is reached.

60.name: bump_bytes
60.docs: Moves to a substring by a number of bytes.

83.name: raw_double_quoted_string
83.docs: Eats the double-quoted string and returns `n_hashes` and an error if encountered.

334.name: NoTerminator
334.docs:
The string was not terminated, e.g. `r###"abcde"##`.
`possible_terminator_offset` is the number of characters after `r` or
`br` where they may have intended to terminate it.

57.name: reset_pos_within_token
57.docs: Resets the number of bytes consumed to 0.

82.name: GuardedStr
82.docs:
`#"abc"#`, `##"a"` (fewer closing), or even `#"a` (unterminated).

Can capture fewer closing hashes than starting hashes,
for more efficient lexing and better backwards diagnostics.

56.name: pos_within_token
56.docs: Returns amount of already consumed symbols.

81.name: guarded_double_quoted_string
81.docs:
Attempt to lex for a guarded string literal.

Used by `rustc_parse::lexer` to lex for guarded strings
conditionally based on edition.

Note: this will not reset the `Cursor` when a
guarded string is not found. It is the caller's
responsibility to do so.

181.name: Unknown
181.docs: Unknown token, not expected by the lexer, e.g. "№"

55.name: is_eof
55.docs: Checks if there is nothing more to consume.

80.name: double_quoted_string
80.docs:
Eats double-quoted string and returns true
if string is terminated.

54.name: third
54.docs: Peeks the third symbol from the input stream without consuming it.

406.name: rustc_lexer
406.docs:
Low-level Rust lexer.

The idea with `rustc_lexer` is to make a reusable library,
by separating out pure lexing and rustc-specific concerns, like spans,
error reporting, and interning. So, rustc_lexer operates directly on `&str`,
produces simple tokens which are a pair of type-tag and a bit of original text,
and does not report errors, instead storing them as flags on the token.

Tokens produced by this lexer are not yet ready for parsing the Rust syntax.
For that see [`rustc_parse::lexer`], which converts this basic token stream
into wide tokens used by actual parser.

The purpose of this crate is to convert raw sources into a labeled sequence
of well-known token types, so building an actual Rust token stream will
be easier.

The main entity of this crate is the [`TokenKind`] enum which represents common
lexeme types.

[`rustc_parse::lexer`]: ../rustc_parse/lexer/index.html

330.name: InvalidStarter
330.docs: Non `#` characters exist between `r` and `"`, e.g. `r##~"abcde"##`

53.name: second
53.docs: Peeks the second symbol from the input stream without consuming it.

405.name: is_ident
405.docs: The passed string is lexically an identifier.

52.name: first
52.docs:
Peeks the next symbol from the input stream without consuming it.
If requested position doesn't exist, `EOF_CHAR` is returned.
However, getting `EOF_CHAR` doesn't always mean actual end of file,
it should be checked with `is_eof` method.

404.name: is_id_continue
404.docs:
True if `c` is valid as a non-first character of an identifier.
See [Rust language reference](https://doc.rust-lang.org/reference/identifiers.html) for
a formal definition of valid identifier name.

51.name: prev
51.docs:
Returns the last eaten symbol (or `'\0'` in release builds).
(For debug assertions only.)

76.name: LiteralKind
76.docs:
Enum representing the literal types supported by the lexer.

Note that the suffix is *not* considered when deciding the `LiteralKind` in
this type. This means that float literals like `1f32` are classified by this
type as `Int`. (Compare against `rustc_ast::token::LitKind` and
`rustc_ast::ast::LitKind`).

403.name: is_id_start
403.docs:
True if `c` is valid as a first character of an identifier.
See [Rust language reference](https://doc.rust-lang.org/reference/identifiers.html) for
a formal definition of valid identifier name.
